SM64DS engine class reference

Every class the ROM's RTTI names, its real inheritance, and what the names mean. Generated from build/rtti.json — read out of the binary, not transcribed. Glosses come from config/rom-name-glossary.json and are the only hand-authored part of this page.

429classes
413inheritance edges
0unresolved
11076virtual slots
10984slots named
10324slots enrolled

How much of this is proven?

This page's reason to exist. Each row is a different claim with a different strength, so they are reported separately rather than averaged into a score. Everything here is joined at generation time — no number below is typed by hand.

claimcountofwhat makes it true
Class exists and is named429429100.0%The ROM stores the name string itself. Read, not inferred.
Base class known413413100.0%A pointer in the typeinfo record. 183 of these cross an overlay boundary.
Vtable located42642999.3%Bound to the record and bounded by the next table, not by a fixed window.
Virtual slot resolves to a named function109841102199.7%Slot word → config/**/symbols.txt in the vtable's own module, or arm9.
…and that function has a source file109731102199.6%tools/srcpath.py resolves the symbol to a path under src/.
…and that file is enrolled in the ROM build103241102193.7%Compiled to an object and linked; the rebuilt ROM is byte-identical to retail.

ROM build at generation time: PASS, 106/106 modules exact (100.000000%), 0 differing bytes of 3049600 compared, 10699 enrolled files. Every enrolled mark on this page inherits that gate.

tierclassesmeaning
every virtual byte-verified80Every non-pure slot resolves to a symbol whose source file is enrolled in the ROM build. The class's whole virtual interface is reproduced byte-for-byte at link time.
some virtuals byte-verified345The interface is fully read out of the ROM and some of its slots are enrolled; the rest are named functions that are not in the link.
interface read, no code enrolled0Every slot resolves to a named function, so the ordered virtual interface is known exactly -- but none of those functions is enrolled.
record only0The typeinfo record is read from the ROM. Some or all of the vtable could not be walked out to named functions.
vtable located, 0 slots read1A vtable address is bound to the record but the slot walk returned nothing. Distinct from having no vtable, and worth a look.
no vtable reachable3The record exists but no vtable could be bound to it. rtti_vtables.py refuses to guess rather than pick a plausible one.

Where the repo's own naming is imprecise

The join between what this repo calls a class and what the ROM calls it, from tools/rtti_reconcile.py. Note the row that matters most: zero outright disagreements. Where the repo falls short it names a true ancestor instead of the immediate base — imprecise, not wrong.

verdictclassesmeaning
unknown_class174no _ZTV symbol — the repo has never named this class
agree157the repo's base is the ROM's base
no_belief71repo knows the class but placed no base
flattened18repo named a true ANCESTOR, skipping the real parent
root_both5both agree it is a root
unproven_name3no corroborated ROM counterpart for the repo's name
agree_primary_only1repo has the offset-0 base and omits the rest

The 18 flattened classes — each one hides a real intermediate class with real shared fields: daBDonketu_c, daDonketu_c, daDsn_c, daObjBSwdoor_c, daObjBk_Fall_Block_c, daObjCvShutter_c, daObjFlMaruta_c, daObjFl_Gura_c, daObjFl_Ukiyuka_c, daObjHmMaruta_c, daObjKm1_Dorifu_c, daObjKm1_Kuruma_c, daObjKm2_Fall_Block_c, daObjKm2_Gura_c, daObjKm3_Dorifu_c, daObjKm3_Kaitendai_c, daObjRc_Dorifu_c, daObjWc_Obj07_c

The honest read: the interface is solved and the fields are not. 10984 of 11021 virtual slots in the entire game resolve to a named function, and 10324 of those are already byte-verified in the link. What no row above claims is field names, types or offsets — RTTI does not carry them, and a wrong field type is usually invisible in the bytes. See notes/runbook-type-reconstruction.md.

The engine's shape

fBase_c is the root of everything — and note that dScene_c and dView_c are siblings of dActor_c, not descendants. Nothing at that level is actor-specific, which is why the tree's name for it (ActorBase) misleads.

429 classes across 19 separate hierarchies. The bar is enrolled / has-source / named over that class's own non-pure vtable slots; the italic name is what this repo calls the class today.

How to read a name

The names are structured. A domain letter, a subsystem, sometimes a two-letter course code, then Japanese romaji describing what the thing is.

Domain letter

tokenmeaningconfidenceevidence
dgame layerhighThe bulk of the engine. dBase_c sits directly under fBase_c.
fframework layerhighfBase_c is the root of everything, including scenes and cameras, not just actors.
mlibrary / middlewarehighOnly mHeap::Heap_t and its two children appear in this ROM's RTTI.
cshared, non-game-specificmediumSeen only on the cMgSmartball_* family in ov006.

What this does not tell you

RTTI carries class names, the inheritance graph, and multiple-inheritance base offsets. It does not carry field names, field types, field offsets, or method names. A class with no virtual functions emits no record and is invisible here. See notes/rtti-reconciliation.md for the full derivation, the traps, and what was deliberately not landed.

Two limits worth stating precisely, because they bound what the green above is worth:

  • A named slot is not a named method. The join proves slot n holds the function at that address and that the tree has a symbol for it. Where that symbol is a func_* placeholder the position is right and the name is still unknown — and a vtable never carries a signature, so parameters and return types come from the definition or from nowhere.
  • Enrolled means the bytes are right, not that the C++ is idiomatic. Most enrolled files are still int*-and-array-index C. Turning them into real methods is what notes/plan-cpp-language-mode.md tracks; for destructors specifically it is currently blocked, and notes/dtor-variant-audit.md §7 has the reason — eligible.py rejects the three-.text object a ~Class() definition always emits.
